_note: THE MILITARY FAMILY, 10 OF ~10: THE DESERTER.
A soldier walked out of the site and will not go back in. Her discharge papers are still inside, in the office of
the officer who kept them. Talk to her at the door, deal with the officer, fetch the papers, and she radios you
when you have them. The verb is RETURN, to someone who left. The talk is FIRST, outside, so she is never inside.
Written to the delve marker set (outside entrance, centre, item markers, boss, wounded) on his ruling, so the
lint pool is EMPTY on military sites until the markers are on them (missionboard06a's note says why).
Every word holds at any military site: nothing names the site, the faction or the weather; everything the lines
point at is placed. Pay: med, capped.

place._theme: Military sites; the family's marker set.

prose.name: Discharge: Deserter's Papers on <Planet>
prose.briefing: A soldier walked out of the <Place> and won't go back in. Her discharge papers are still inside.
prose.card: Private contract. A former soldier is waiting outside the <Place> on <Planet>. Recover her discharge papers from inside. Discretion appreciated. Payment on contract completion.

beats.objective: Talk to the soldier outside the <Place>
beats.journal: The soldier outside the <Place> walked out and won't go back. Her discharge papers are inside, with the officer who kept them.

person.name: Corporal Mabry
hellos: I'm not going back in. Whatever you've heard.

greeting: If you've read the posting, you know I walked out. My discharge papers are still in there. The officer wouldn't sign them, so I signed myself out.

reply: They're in her office, in a case. She'll be in there with them. She doesn't trust anyone else near paperwork.
Because she would have kept us here until there was nobody left to keep. I'd rather be the one who left than one of the ones who didn't.

exchanges.prompt: What happens if you go back?
reply: Nothing good, and nothing fast. So I'll wait here, thanks.

beats._talk: Exchange 0 ends the talk and sets the next stage. Every prompt stands on the greeting. Voice 'Verity', british, unused so far; the same voice on the radio.

beats.journal: The officer at the <Place> won't be keeping anyone else here. Her office is open now.
say: Is she...? Right. The papers are in her office, so bring them out to me.

beats.journal: A soldier walked out of the <Place> and wouldn't go back. I dealt with the officer who kept her there and found her discharge papers, under eleven more nobody had signed either.
beats.name: Officer's Case

message.title: Discharge Papers
message.text: Hers, on top, with the signature box empty. Under them, eleven more just like it.

say: That's all of them. So I'm not a deserter any more. I'm just someone who left.

broadcast: You're close? I'm outside, by the door. I'm not going in. Come and talk to me first.
_speech: On a board the broadcast waits for him at the site. Not yet heard in game; his ear decides. No names, places, factions or currency in a voiced line.
